'''Dipendra Prasad''' (born 1960)<ref name="insa">{{cite web | url=http://insaindia.org.in/detail.php?id=P03-1342 | archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20160812230500/http://insaindia.org.in/detail.php?id=P03-1342 | archive-date=12 August 2016 | title=Indian Fellow: Professor Dipendra Prasad | publisher=[[Indian National Science Academy]] | accessdate=3 January 2013|url-status=usurped}}</ref> is an Indian mathematician.  He is an Emeritus Fellow of mathematics at the [[Indian Institute of Technology Bombay]]. He is a [[number theorist]] known for his work in the areas of [[automorphic representations]] and the [[Gan–Gross–Prasad conjecture]].<ref>{{Citation | last1=Gan | first1=Wee Teck | last2=Gross | first2=Benedict H. | last3=Prasad | first3=Dipendra | chapter=Symplectic local root numbers, central critical L-values, and restriction problems in the representation theory of classical groups | mr=3202556 | year=2012 | title=[[Astérisque]] | isbn=978-2-85629-348-5 | volume=346 | pages=1–109}}</ref><ref name="b">{{cite web|url=http://www.kurims.kyoto-u.ac.jp/~kyodo/kokyuroku/contents/pdf/1338-17.pdf|access-date=2017-03-11|date=2003|title=Restriction of Hermitian Maas Lifts and the Gross-Prasad Conjecture}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.ams.org/bookstore-getitem/item=AST-346|title = American Mathematical Society Home}}</ref> He was the president of Commission for Developing Countries (CDC) of [[International Mathematical Union]] (2018–2022)<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.mathunion.org/organization/imu-leadership-2019-2022|title=IMU Leadership 2019 – 2022 &#124; International Mathematical Union (IMU)}}</ref> and of Indian Math Society (2021–2022).<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.indianmathsociety.org.in/thecouncil.htm|title=Thecouncil}}</ref> Presently, he is the Chairman of the National 
Board of Higher Mathematics (NBHM) in India.

Two of his siblings, [[Gopal Prasad]] and [[Shrawan Kumar (mathematician)|Shrawan Kumar]], are also mathematicians.

==Education==
Prasad obtained his [[bachelor's degree]] from the [[St. Xavier's College, Mumbai]] in 1978 before moving to the [[Indian Institute of Technology Kanpur]] for a [[Master's degree|Masters]] which he completed in 1980.<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://iitk.ac.in/dora/profile/Dr-Dipendra-Prasad|title = Dr Dipendra Prasad}}</ref> From 1980–1985, Prasad worked as a research scholar at the Tata Institute of Fundamental Research, Mumbai (TIFR Mumbai).<ref name="tifr-home"/> He then completed his PhD under the supervision of [[Benedict Gross]] at Harvard, in 1989.<ref name="tifr-home"/><ref>{{MathGenealogy|id=30163}}</ref>

==Career==
From 1989–1997, Prasad was a research assistant, fellow, and then reader at TIFR Mumbai.<ref name="tifr-home"/> From 1992–1993, Prasad was a member of the [[Institute for Advanced Study]].<ref name="tifr-home"/> From 1994–2004, Prasad was an associate professor and then full professor at the [[Harish-Chandra Research Institute]] in [[Allahabad]].<ref name="tifr-home"/> From 2004 until 2019, Prasad was a professor at TIFR Mumbai.<ref name="tifr-home">{{cite web|title=D. Prasad |last=Prasad |first=Dipendra |url=http://www.math.tifr.res.in/~dprasad/#exp |accessdate=27 September 2019}}</ref> In 2019, Prasad moved to the Indian Institute of Technology Bombay.<ref>{{cite web|url=http://iitb.ac.in/en/employee/prof-dipendra-prasad |title=Prof. Dipendra Prasad |website=Indian Institute of Technology Bombay |accessdate=27 September 2019}}</ref>

==Awards==
In recognition of his contributions, the [[Government of India]] awarded him the [[Shanti Swarup Bhatnagar Prize for Science and Technology|Shanti Swarup Bhatnagar Prize]] in [[mathematical sciences]] for 2002. In 2010 he was awarded the JC Bose of the [[Department of Science and Technology (India)|Department of Science and Technology]], New Delhi.<ref>{{Cite web|url=http://www.tifr.res.in/Notices/search.php?sp=20&past=Y&appid=awardshonours_notices|title = Tata Institute of Fundamental Research &#124; TIFR|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20131105025410/https://www.tifr.res.in/Notices/search.php?sp=20&past=Y&appid=awardshonours_notices|archive-date=2013-11-05|url-status=unfit}}</ref> He is also a recipient of the Swarna Jayanti Fellowship in 1999.<ref name="insa"/> He was Invited Speaker on the [[International Congress of Mathematicians]] 2018 in [[Rio de Janeiro]] in Section 7 (Lie Groups and Generalizations) with the talk 'Ext-analogues of branching laws'.

* Srinivasa Ramanujan Birth Centenary Award of The Indian Science Congress Association (ISCA), 2005.{{citation needed|date=December 2025}}
